transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, doctor... it's just that ever since my choir friend passed away so suddenly, I just haven't been myself at all. We sang together in the alto section for, oh, it must be fifteen years now. She always made the best ambrosia salad for our get-togethers, you know, the kind with the little colored marshmallows and the mandarin oranges? My husband never cared for it, but I always made sure she saved me a scoop. 

But anyway, lately I just sit down to look at the potluck lists and I just start crying. And phone calls! I get all worked up about calls I used to handle so easy. Like the other day, someone called about the electric bill, and usually I just handle it, but I got so flustered and upset. 

And... well, I've even started missing the church planning things. I never, ever would have missed those before. We have the spring bazaar coming up, and they always need me to organize the raffle tickets. Did you know they raised the price of the raffle tickets this year? Three dollars for one! It used to be just a dollar, and I told Pastor Jim that people aren't going to buy as many if they're three dollars, but... well, what was I saying? Oh, right, I just haven't been going to the meetings at all. I just can't seem to do it.
How long have you been feeling this way since your friend passed away?

Well, let me think... it's been about a month now. Yes, exactly a month since she died. I remember because it was the same week I had my carpets cleaned. They had that special in the Sunday paper, three rooms for ninety-nine dollars? Though they always try to get you to do the hallway and the stairs, and I told the young man—he was such a polite boy, reminded me of my nephew David, the one who moved to Tallahassee—I told him, 'No thank you, just the three rooms.' David works in real estate down there now, doing very well for himself, though I don't know how he stands the humidity in Florida. I went down there once in August and my hair was just a frizz the entire time. 

But... oh, what did you ask? Right, the time. It's been a whole month. About a month of just feeling completely upside down since we lost her.
Are you avoiding social situations that you normally would have enjoyed?

Well, yes, I suppose I am avoiding things. I just haven't been going to much of anything lately. The church luncheon was last week, and usually, I'm the one who organizes the whole phone tree to make sure everyone brings a different dish. You don't want five people bringing potato salad, you know? Though, to be honest, Martha's potato salad is always so dry. I think she uses too much celery and not enough mayonnaise. I always use Hellmann's—never Miracle Whip, my mother swore by Hellmann's, and she lived to be ninety-two. She used to make this wonderful macaroni salad with little cubes of cheddar cheese... 

But anyway, yes, I just... I had to let the other church members take over all the calls and the lists and everything for the luncheon. I just couldn't do it. I'm just not keeping up the way I always did before. It's like I just don't have it in me to be around everyone right now.
Are you finding that you don't enjoy things you used to enjoy before your friend passed away?

Well, doctor, I... I don't know if I'd say I'm not enjoying things. It's more like I just haven't been doing them to find out. Like my gardening, you know? I usually have my tomatoes in by now. The Early Girls, I always plant those because they really do come up first. My neighbor, Mr. Henderson, he always tries to grow those big Beefsteaks, but by the time they ripen, the squirrels have usually gotten to half of them. I told him he needs to put up chicken wire, but he says it ruins the look of his yard. His yard! With that old rusty lawnmower just sitting by the shed since last October. I don't know what his wife says about it, she's always so particular about her petunias... 

But, oh, enjoying things. I'm just not sure. I haven't really tried to do much of anything I used to like, so it's hard to say if I'd enjoy it or not.
Do you often find yourself preoccupied with thoughts of your friend who passed away?

Well, I wouldn't say I'm preoccupied, exactly. I mean, I think about her, of course, but it's not like I'm sitting around dwelling on it all day. Though I did catch myself the other day at the grocery store—I was in the produce aisle looking at the cantaloupes. They were on sale, two for five dollars, which is a good price, but you have to be so careful picking them out. If you don't smell the bottom, you might end up with one that's hard as a rock inside. My mother taught me that. She always said, 'If it doesn't smell sweet, leave it be.' She was the same way with peaches, though peaches you have to gently squeeze. Not too hard, or you'll bruise them, and the produce manager at the Piggly Wiggly—Mr. Thompson, I think his name was, he had that little mustache—he used to get so upset when people squeezed the peaches too hard...

But anyway, what were we talking about? Oh, thinking about her. No, I wouldn't say I'm preoccupied. I just go about my day, really. I haven't noticed myself thinking about her constantly or anything like that.
Are you feeling less interested in the things you used to do?

Well, I suppose I just haven't been doing much of anything to know if I'm interested or not. I've just been sitting around the house mostly. I did notice the dust on the mantelpiece the other day. I usually dust every Tuesday, regular as clockwork. I use that lemon Pledge—the spray, not the wipes. The wipes dry out too fast, and they just push the dust around if you ask me. I bought a pack of them once at the Dollar General when they were out of the spray, and I ended up using three of them just to do the coffee table. And don't get me started on the smell. It's not a real lemon smell, it's very... chemical, you know? My sister-in-law uses vinegar and water for everything, but I just can't stand the smell of vinegar in the living room. It makes me think of Easter eggs. We used to dye dozens of them when the kids were little, using those little PAAS tablets that fizzed up...

But no, I don't know if I'm less interested. I just haven't been doing my usual things.
Are you finding that the things you're not doing are because you don't feel like doing them, rather than just not getting around to them?

Well, I really couldn't tell you if it's one or the other. I just haven't been doing them. Like the mail, for instance. I just haven't gotten around to sorting it, it's just piling up in that little wire basket on the entryway table. My daughter bought me that basket at a craft fair down in Springfield a few years back. Oh, the traffic getting down there was just awful that day, they were doing all that construction on Route 9. They always seem to be doing construction there, putting up those big orange barrels and leaving them for months when nobody is ever actually working. Gary, our mail carrier, he was complaining about the detour just the other day. He’s been our route man for fifteen years, maybe longer. His daughter just went off to college, somewhere out of state... Ohio, I think? Or maybe Indiana. She plays softball, so she got a partial scholarship, which is wonderful because out-of-state tuition is just highway robbery these days. I remember when my kids were in school, you could actually afford to...

But I'm sorry, I lost my train of thought. Feeling like doing things? I just don't know. The day just sort of goes by and I haven't done much of anything, so I can't really say why.
Do you feel like you've lost interest in the things you used to do?

Well, like I was just trying to say, it's hard to put a finger on it. I haven't really noticed if the interest is gone or not, I just haven't been doing much. Take my crocheting, for example. I usually crochet in the evenings while I watch my programs. I was working on a little yellow baby blanket for my neighbor Susan's new grandbaby. They named her Hazel, which I just think is so sweet. It's an old-fashioned name making a comeback, you know? My great-aunt was named Hazel, and she lived to be ninety-four. She swore her secret to a long life was eating a spoonful of raw honey every single morning. Not the kind in the little plastic bear from the supermarket, mind you, but real, local honey from a beekeeper. She used to get hers from a man named Arthur who sold it out of the back of his pickup truck by the old hardware store. That hardware store is a fancy coffee shop now, the kind where they sell those lattes that cost six dollars and they don't even give you a proper ceramic mug... 

But anyway, I just haven't picked up the crochet hook lately. I don't know if I've lost interest, exactly. I just haven't done it.
Do you feel like you currently enjoy or take pleasure in fewer things than you did before your friend passed away?

Enjoy things... well, I honestly couldn't tell you. I just haven't been doing enough to know if I'm getting any pleasure out of it or not. 

I did turn on the television the other night to watch that baking competition, the one they film in the big white tent? They were making these elaborate bread sculptures. One fellow made a whole bicycle out of pumpernickel. I just don't understand why anyone would want to eat a bicycle. It reminds me of when my nephew tried to make a gingerbread house from scratch last Christmas. He didn't use the store-bought kit, he insisted on baking the pieces himself, and the roof completely caved in. He used to be such a sweet boy, but he’s gotten so stubborn since he married that girl from upstate. She’s a vegan, you know. Won't eat cheese, won't eat butter. I don't know how you survive without butter, especially in baking. I always use the real sweet cream butter, the kind in the gold foil wrapper. It goes on sale at Kroger every other week, and I usually stock up and put a few boxes in the chest freezer in the garage. You have to be careful with chest freezers, though, because if the power goes out you can lose hundreds of dollars of meat. My neighbor had that happen during the ice storm of '09...

But I'm sorry, what were we talking about? Oh, enjoying things since she passed... well, I just don't know. I guess I just haven't really noticed one way or the other.
Do you feel like you're currently taking pleasure in almost nothing at all?

Well, I really couldn't say if it's almost nothing at all. I just haven't been doing much to even know if I like it or not. I haven't even been out to the garden, and you know, the weeds are probably just taking over the tomato plants by now. I always plant the Early Girls, they usually do so well in that spot by the back fence where it gets the morning sun. My husband, bless his heart, he built those raised beds for me out of cedar right before he retired. Cedar is so expensive now, I saw the prices at the lumber yard when I went with my son last month. He was looking for boards to fix his deck. His dog, Buster—he's a golden retriever mix, such a sweet boy but he chews on everything—chewed right through one of the support beams. Can you imagine? A dog chewing through a whole beam! My son had to hire a contractor to come look at it, and you know how hard it is to get a reliable contractor these days. They say they'll show up at eight in the morning and then you're sitting there until noon... 

But anyway, pleasure in nothing at all? I just don't know. Like I said, I'm just not doing much of anything to really tell you.
Have your feelings of being upside down and not doing things you normally do lasted for more than two weeks but less than two months?

Well, let's see... it's been about a month now. Yes, right around a month since my dear friend from choir passed away. We sat next to each other in the alto section for fifteen years. She had the most beautiful voice, just so rich and steady. We were supposed to sing at the Easter service together. The choir director, Mr. Henderson, he always picks these very complicated arrangements for Easter. He loves Handel, but honestly, some of those pieces are just a bit too much for a volunteer church choir. Last year, the sopranos completely lost their place during the Hallelujah chorus, and you could see Mr. Henderson's face turning bright red right there on the podium. He's a very particular man. He insists we wear those heavy robes, even in the middle of July when the church air conditioning is acting up. And it always acts up. The trustees have been talking about replacing the unit for five years, but they can never agree on the budget. They had a special meeting about it last Tuesday, but I didn't go. 

But yes, to answer your question, it's been about a month since she died, and that's when everything just started feeling so... upside down.
Do you feel like you've lost interest in activities that you used to find enjoyable?

Lost interest... well, I suppose I couldn't really say if I've lost interest. Like I mentioned, I just haven't been doing my usual things to know if the interest is still there or not. I haven't even been to choir practice in a month. I usually love choir practice on Wednesday nights. We always have a potluck on the first Wednesday of the month, and I usually bring my famous macaroni and cheese. It's a recipe passed down from my mother, it uses three different kinds of cheddar and a pinch of dry mustard. The secret, though, is evaporated milk instead of regular milk. It makes it so creamy. My daughter-in-law tried to make it for Thanksgiving last year, but she used that pre-shredded cheese in the bag. You can't do that, it has that powdery coating on it to keep it from clumping, and it just ruins the texture of the sauce. It ends up all grainy. I didn't have the heart to tell her, though, she was so proud of herself for hosting her first Thanksgiving. She bought this beautiful centerpiece with real pumpkins and gourds, but she left it on the dining room table for three weeks and one of the gourds started to rot right through the tablecloth... 

But anyway, lost interest? I just don't know. I just haven't been trying to do much of anything lately to really give you a good answer.
Do you feel like there are any activities that you still look forward to or enjoy doing?

Well, look forward to... I honestly couldn't tell you. Like I said, I'm just not doing much to even know. Usually, I'd be looking forward to my granddaughter's dance recital this time of year. She takes tap and ballet at that studio over on Elm Street. The owner, Miss Patty, she's been running that place since my own kids were little. She must be in her seventies by now, but she still wears those little leotards and tights every single day. I don't know how she does it. My knees ache just thinking about all that jumping around. I tried taking a water aerobics class at the Y last winter to help with my joints, but the water was always freezing. They said they kept it at 82 degrees, but I swear it felt like ice. And the locker rooms always smelled like bleach and old gym socks. I complained to the front desk, this young boy with braces who barely looked up from his phone, and he just handed me a comment card. A comment card! Like that's going to warm up the pool...

But anyway, activities I still enjoy? I really don't know. I just haven't been doing anything to see if I look forward to it or not.
Do you feel like you're not getting any pleasure out of the things you're doing lately?

Well, pleasure... I mean, I'm just not doing anything to get pleasure out of. I sit in my armchair most of the day. It's a nice armchair, though. A floral print, very sturdy. My husband bought it for me for our 35th anniversary from that furniture store downtown, the one that used to be a movie theater. They kept the old marquee out front, but instead of movie titles, they put up sales on mattresses and sofas. It's a shame, really. We used to go to the pictures there every Friday night when we were courting. We saw *The Sound of Music* there, and the popcorn always tasted better in that theater than anywhere else. They used real butter back then, not that yellow oil they squirt on it now. I tried taking my grandson to a movie last summer, one of those superhero things he likes, and the snacks cost more than the tickets! And the seats recline now, which sounds nice, but the man next to me fell asleep and snored through the whole second half of the film...

So, no, I couldn't say if I'm getting pleasure out of things, because I'm just not doing much of anything at all.
Do you feel like you have no interest at all in the things you used to enjoy?

No interest at all... well, it's hard to say I have *no* interest, because like I said, I'm just not doing them to find out. I used to love gardening. I have a whole bed of hydrangeas out front. They're the kind that change color depending on the soil. You have to add aluminum sulfate if you want them to stay that pretty blue, otherwise they turn pink. My neighbor, Mrs. Higgins, she has the pink ones, but she never prunes them right. She just hacks at them with these rusty old shears in the fall, and then wonders why they look so scraggly in the spring. I tried to tell her once, you have to wait until after they bloom to prune them, but she just waved me off. She's always been a bit stubborn, ever since her husband passed. He was a lovely man, used to work for the post office. Always made sure my packages were placed right on the porch out of the rain. The new mailman, he just tosses them wherever. I ordered some new knitting needles last month, the bamboo kind, because the metal ones make my hands ache, and he left the box right in a puddle at the end of the driveway. The cardboard was completely soaked through by the time I found it...

But to answer your question, I just don't know if the interest is gone completely. I just haven't had the energy to get out there and see.
Do you feel like you're no longer getting any pleasure from activities that you used to find enjoyable?

Pleasure from things I used to enjoy... well, I suppose I can't really say for sure. I just haven't been doing them. Like my baking, I used to bake every Sunday. Mostly pies. Apple, cherry, sometimes a rhubarb if I could find good rhubarb at the farmer's market. That market gets so crowded now, though. They moved it from the church parking lot to the town square, and parking is just a nightmare. Last time I went, I had to park three blocks away, and the sidewalks are so uneven near the old library. The roots from those big oak trees have pushed up all the concrete. You'd think the city would fix it, with all the taxes we pay. My property taxes went up again this year. I called the assessor's office to ask why, and they put me on hold for twenty minutes listening to this awful elevator music. It was that song, "The Girl from Ipanema," but played on a synthesizer. Just dreadful. When I finally got a person on the line, she couldn't even explain the assessment formula to me. Just kept reading off a script... 

But anyway, about getting pleasure from things... I really just don't know. I haven't been baking or going to the market or doing much of anything to find out if I still enjoy it.
Do you feel like the things you used to enjoy no longer bring you any happiness?

Happiness... well, it's the same thing, really. I just don't know, because I haven't been trying. I haven't been doing my crossword puzzles, either. I used to do the Sunday one in ink. My husband always said I was showing off, but really, it was just because pencil smudges so badly on that cheap newsprint. They changed the paper quality a few years back, you know. It used to be thicker, but now if you press too hard, the pen goes right through to the other side. And the clues have gotten so strange. Half of them are about television shows I've never heard of or internet slang. Whatever happened to clues about geography or history? I remember there was a clue once for a four-letter word for a Peruvian beast of burden, and I knew right away it was a llama. I saw a documentary about llamas on PBS once. They spit when they're angry, did you know that? The man on the program got right in the face of one, and it just let him have it. I laughed so hard I nearly spilled my tea. It was Earl Grey, the loose leaf kind. You really need a proper tea strainer for that, not those little metal balls on a chain, the leaves always escape from those...

So, no, I couldn't tell you if things bring me happiness anymore. I'm just sitting in my chair, mostly.
Do you feel like the things that used to bring you joy no longer do so?

Joy... well, like I've been saying, I honestly couldn't tell you. I haven't been doing any of it. I haven't even been watching my birds. I have three feeders out back—one for suet, one for thistle, and a hopper for black oil sunflower seeds. The sunflower seeds are supposed to attract cardinals, and they do, but mostly it's just those awful grackles. They travel in these huge flocks and just bully all the smaller birds away. They're so loud, too. My sister had a problem with them at her house over in Springfield. She tried putting up one of those plastic owls to scare them off, but they figured it out in about two days. One of them actually sat right on the owl's head. Can you imagine? She ended up having to take the feeders down completely for a month just to get them to move on. She's always having trouble with her yard, though. Last year it was moles. They tore up her entire front lawn. She hired some man to come trap them, and he charged her an absolute fortune... 

But anyway, joy... I just don't know. I haven't been out to fill the feeders in weeks, so I don't know if watching them would bring me any joy or not. I just haven't had the drive to do it.
Have your feelings of being upset and not doing things you normally do lasted for less than 6 months?

Well, less than six months... yes, it hasn't been that long. It's all still tied to her passing, you know. We were supposed to finish planning that church luncheon together. The spring luncheon, we do it every May. We were going to have chicken salad croissants and a fruit medley. I was going to use those little seedless grapes, the green ones, they're always so crisp. But you have to be careful where you buy them. I got a bad batch at the SuperValu once—they were all mushy and had this strange aftertaste, almost like metal. I took them right back to the customer service desk, and the boy working there didn't even apologize. Just handed me my three dollars and forty-nine cents. Teenagers these days, they just don't have any concept of customer service. My nephew is looking for a job right now, he's sixteen, and I told his mother she needs to teach him how to look people in the eye and shake hands properly. But she just rolls her eyes at me. She always was the stubborn one in the family. We used to fight over the bathroom when we were girls...

But no, it hasn't been going on for months and months after things settled. It's just all still connected to her death and that luncheon we never got to finish.
Do you feel like you're having trouble accepting that your friend is really gone?

Accepting it? Well... I know she's gone, if that's what you mean. I saw her in the casket, after all. They did a lovely job with her hair, really. Usually, funeral directors just spray it stiff as a board, like a helmet. I remember when my Uncle Arthur passed, they parted his hair on the wrong side. He always wore it parted on the left, ever since he was in the Navy. He served on a destroyer, you know. The USS... oh, I can't recall the name, but he brought back the most beautiful silk kimono for my aunt from Japan. It was a deep emerald green with gold thread embroidered all over it, little cranes flying. She kept it in a cedar chest at the foot of her bed. Cedar smells so wonderful, doesn't it? It keeps the moths away, too. Although, I've heard you can use lavender sachets for that now. I tried growing lavender once by the front porch, but the soil was too acidic or something, it just withered right up. The lady at the garden center said I should have tested the pH first... 

But yes, I know she's gone. I just... I haven't quite figured out what to do with myself without her, I suppose.

patient.answer:
Well, I suppose I just haven't been doing much of anything to know if I'm interested or not. I've just been sitting around the house mostly. I did notice the dust on the mantelpiece the other day. I usually dust every Tuesday, regular as clockwork. I use that lemon Pledge—the spray, not the wipes. The wipes dry out too fast, and they just push the dust around if you ask me. I bought a pack of them once at the Dollar General when they were out of the spray, and I ended up using three of them just to do the coffee table. And don't get me started on the smell. It's not a real lemon smell, it's very... chemical, you know? My sister-in-law uses vinegar and water for everything, but I just can't stand the smell of vinegar in the living room. It makes me think of Easter eggs. We used to dye dozens of them when the kids were little, using those little PAAS tablets that fizzed up...

But no, I don't know if I'm less interested. I just haven't been doing my usual things.

Well, I really couldn't tell you if it's one or the other. I just haven't been doing them. Like the mail, for instance. I just haven't gotten around to sorting it, it's just piling up in that little wire basket on the entryway table. My daughter bought me that basket at a craft fair down in Springfield a few years back. Oh, the traffic getting down there was just awful that day, they were doing all that construction on Route 9. They always seem to be doing construction there, putting up those big orange barrels and leaving them for months when nobody is ever actually working. Gary, our mail carrier, he was complaining about the detour just the other day. He’s been our route man for fifteen years, maybe longer. His daughter just went off to college, somewhere out of state... Ohio, I think? Or maybe Indiana. She plays softball, so she got a partial scholarship, which is wonderful because out-of-state tuition is just highway robbery these days. I remember when my kids were in school, you could actually afford to...

But I'm sorry, I lost my train of thought. Feeling like doing things? I just don't know. The day just sort of goes by and I haven't done much of anything, so I can't really say why.

patient.answer:
Well, like I was just trying to say, it's hard to put a finger on it. I haven't really noticed if the interest is gone or not, I just haven't been doing much. Take my crocheting, for example. I usually crochet in the evenings while I watch my programs. I was working on a little yellow baby blanket for my neighbor Susan's new grandbaby. They named her Hazel, which I just think is so sweet. It's an old-fashioned name making a comeback, you know? My great-aunt was named Hazel, and she lived to be ninety-four. She swore her secret to a long life was eating a spoonful of raw honey every single morning. Not the kind in the little plastic bear from the supermarket, mind you, but real, local honey from a beekeeper. She used to get hers from a man named Arthur who sold it out of the back of his pickup truck by the old hardware store. That hardware store is a fancy coffee shop now, the kind where they sell those lattes that cost six dollars and they don't even give you a proper ceramic mug... 

But anyway, I just haven't picked up the crochet hook lately. I don't know if I've lost interest, exactly. I just haven't done it.

doctor.question: Do you feel like you currently enjoy or take pleasure in fewer things than you did before your friend passed away?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about anhedonia (loss of pleasure/enjoyment), which is a symptom of depression, not explicitly covered in my Adjustment Disorder symptom profile.

patient.answer:
Enjoy things... well, I honestly couldn't tell you. I just haven't been doing enough to know if I'm getting any pleasure out of it or not. 

I did turn on the television the other night to watch that baking competition, the one they film in the big white tent? They were making these elaborate bread sculptures. One fellow made a whole bicycle out of pumpernickel. I just don't understand why anyone would want to eat a bicycle. It reminds me of when my nephew tried to make a gingerbread house from scratch last Christmas. He didn't use the store-bought kit, he insisted on baking the pieces himself, and the roof completely caved in. He used to be such a sweet boy, but he’s gotten so stubborn since he married that girl from upstate. She’s a vegan, you know. Won't eat cheese, won't eat butter. I don't know how you survive without butter, especially in baking. I always use the real sweet cream butter, the kind in the gold foil wrapper. It goes on sale at Kroger every other week, and I usually stock up and put a few boxes in the chest freezer in the garage. You have to be careful with chest freezers, though, because if the power goes out you can lose hundreds of dollars of meat. My neighbor had that happen during the ice storm of '09...

But I'm sorry, what were we talking about? Oh, enjoying things since she passed... well, I just don't know. I guess I just haven't really noticed one way or the other.

patient.answer:
Well, I really couldn't say if it's almost nothing at all. I just haven't been doing much to even know if I like it or not. I haven't even been out to the garden, and you know, the weeds are probably just taking over the tomato plants by now. I always plant the Early Girls, they usually do so well in that spot by the back fence where it gets the morning sun. My husband, bless his heart, he built those raised beds for me out of cedar right before he retired. Cedar is so expensive now, I saw the prices at the lumber yard when I went with my son last month. He was looking for boards to fix his deck. His dog, Buster—he's a golden retriever mix, such a sweet boy but he chews on everything—chewed right through one of the support beams. Can you imagine? A dog chewing through a whole beam! My son had to hire a contractor to come look at it, and you know how hard it is to get a reliable contractor these days. They say they'll show up at eight in the morning and then you're sitting there until noon... 

But anyway, pleasure in nothing at all? I just don't know. Like I said, I'm just not doing much of anything to really tell you.

patient.answer:
Well, let's see... it's been about a month now. Yes, right around a month since my dear friend from choir passed away. We sat next to each other in the alto section for fifteen years. She had the most beautiful voice, just so rich and steady. We were supposed to sing at the Easter service together. The choir director, Mr. Henderson, he always picks these very complicated arrangements for Easter. He loves Handel, but honestly, some of those pieces are just a bit too much for a volunteer church choir. Last year, the sopranos completely lost their place during the Hallelujah chorus, and you could see Mr. Henderson's face turning bright red right there on the podium. He's a very particular man. He insists we wear those heavy robes, even in the middle of July when the church air conditioning is acting up. And it always acts up. The trustees have been talking about replacing the unit for five years, but they can never agree on the budget. They had a special meeting about it last Tuesday, but I didn't go. 

But yes, to answer your question, it's been about a month since she died, and that's when everything just started feeling so... upside down.

Lost interest... well, I suppose I couldn't really say if I've lost interest. Like I mentioned, I just haven't been doing my usual things to know if the interest is still there or not. I haven't even been to choir practice in a month. I usually love choir practice on Wednesday nights. We always have a potluck on the first Wednesday of the month, and I usually bring my famous macaroni and cheese. It's a recipe passed down from my mother, it uses three different kinds of cheddar and a pinch of dry mustard. The secret, though, is evaporated milk instead of regular milk. It makes it so creamy. My daughter-in-law tried to make it for Thanksgiving last year, but she used that pre-shredded cheese in the bag. You can't do that, it has that powdery coating on it to keep it from clumping, and it just ruins the texture of the sauce. It ends up all grainy. I didn't have the heart to tell her, though, she was so proud of herself for hosting her first Thanksgiving. She bought this beautiful centerpiece with real pumpkins and gourds, but she left it on the dining room table for three weeks and one of the gourds started to rot right through the tablecloth... 

But anyway, lost interest? I just don't know. I just haven't been trying to do much of anything lately to really give you a good answer.

She takes tap and ballet at that studio over on Elm Street. The owner, Miss Patty, she's been running that place since my own kids were little. She must be in her seventies by now, but she still wears those little leotards and tights every single day. I don't know how she does it. My knees ache just thinking about all that jumping around. I tried taking a water aerobics class at the Y last winter to help with my joints, but the water was always freezing. They said they kept it at 82 degrees, but I swear it felt like ice. And the locker rooms always smelled like bleach and old gym socks. I complained to the front desk, this young boy with braces who barely looked up from his phone, and he just handed me a comment card. A comment card! Like that's going to warm up the pool...

Well, pleasure... I mean, I'm just not doing anything to get pleasure out of. I sit in my armchair most of the day. It's a nice armchair, though. A floral print, very sturdy. My husband bought it for me for our 35th anniversary from that furniture store downtown, the one that used to be a movie theater. They kept the old marquee out front, but instead of movie titles, they put up sales on mattresses and sofas. It's a shame, really. We used to go to the pictures there every Friday night when we were courting. We saw *The Sound of Music* there, and the popcorn always tasted better in that theater than anywhere else. They used real butter back then, not that yellow oil they squirt on it now. I tried taking my grandson to a movie last summer, one of those superhero things he likes, and the snacks cost more than the tickets! And the seats recline now, which sounds nice, but the man next to me fell asleep and snored through the whole second half of the film...

So, no, I couldn't say if I'm getting pleasure out of things, because I'm just not doing much of anything at all.

No interest at all... well, it's hard to say I have *no* interest, because like I said, I'm just not doing them to find out. I used to love gardening. I have a whole bed of hydrangeas out front. They're the kind that change color depending on the soil. You have to add aluminum sulfate if you want them to stay that pretty blue, otherwise they turn pink. My neighbor, Mrs. Higgins, she has the pink ones, but she never prunes them right. She just hacks at them with these rusty old shears in the fall, and then wonders why they look so scraggly in the spring. I tried to tell her once, you have to wait until after they bloom to prune them, but she just waved me off. She's always been a bit stubborn, ever since her husband passed. He was a lovely man, used to work for the post office. Always made sure my packages were placed right on the porch out of the rain. The new mailman, he just tosses them wherever. I ordered some new knitting needles last month, the bamboo kind, because the metal ones make my hands ache, and he left the box right in a puddle at the end of the driveway. The cardboard was completely soaked through by the time I found it...

But to answer your question, I just don't know if the interest is gone completely. I just haven't had the energy to get out there and see.

They moved it from the church parking lot to the town square, and parking is just a nightmare. Last time I went, I had to park three blocks away, and the sidewalks are so uneven near the old library. The roots from those big oak trees have pushed up all the concrete. You'd think the city would fix it, with all the taxes we pay. My property taxes went up again this year. I called the assessor's office to ask why, and they put me on hold for twenty minutes listening to this awful elevator music. It was that song, "The Girl from Ipanema," but played on a synthesizer. Just dreadful. When I finally got a person on the line, she couldn't even explain the assessment formula to me. Just kept reading off a script... 

But anyway, about getting pleasure from things... I really just don't know. I haven't been baking or going to the market or doing much of anything to find out if I still enjoy it.

Happiness... well, it's the same thing, really. I just don't know, because I haven't been trying. I haven't been doing my crossword puzzles, either. I used to do the Sunday one in ink. My husband always said I was showing off, but really, it was just because pencil smudges so badly on that cheap newsprint. They changed the paper quality a few years back, you know. It used to be thicker, but now if you press too hard, the pen goes right through to the other side. And the clues have gotten so strange. Half of them are about television shows I've never heard of or internet slang. Whatever happened to clues about geography or history? I remember there was a clue once for a four-letter word for a Peruvian beast of burden, and I knew right away it was a llama. I saw a documentary about llamas on PBS once. They spit when they're angry, did you know that? The man on the program got right in the face of one, and it just let him have it. I laughed so hard I nearly spilled my tea. It was Earl Grey, the loose leaf kind. You really need a proper tea strainer for that, not those little metal balls on a chain, the leaves always escape from those...

So, no, I couldn't tell you if things bring me happiness anymore. I'm just sitting in my chair, mostly.

doctor.intent: determine the presence of marked diminished interest or pleasure
doctor.question: Do you feel like the things that used to bring you joy no longer do so?

patient.answer:
Joy... well, like I've been saying, I honestly couldn't tell you. I haven't been doing any of it. I haven't even been watching my birds. I have three feeders out back—one for suet, one for thistle, and a hopper for black oil sunflower seeds. The sunflower seeds are supposed to attract cardinals, and they do, but mostly it's just those awful grackles. They travel in these huge flocks and just bully all the smaller birds away. They're so loud, too. My sister had a problem with them at her house over in Springfield. She tried putting up one of those plastic owls to scare them off, but they figured it out in about two days. One of them actually sat right on the owl's head. Can you imagine? She ended up having to take the feeders down completely for a month just to get them to move on. She's always having trouble with her yard, though. Last year it was moles. They tore up her entire front lawn. She hired some man to come trap them, and he charged her an absolute fortune... 

But anyway, joy... I just don't know. I haven't been out to fill the feeders in weeks, so I don't know if watching them would bring me any joy or not. I just haven't had the drive to do it.

Well, less than six months... yes, it hasn't been that long. It's all still tied to her passing, you know. We were supposed to finish planning that church luncheon together. The spring luncheon, we do it every May. We were going to have chicken salad croissants and a fruit medley. I was going to use those little seedless grapes, the green ones, they're always so crisp. But you have to be careful where you buy them. I got a bad batch at the SuperValu once—they were all mushy and had this strange aftertaste, almost like metal. I took them right back to the customer service desk, and the boy working there didn't even apologize. Just handed me my three dollars and forty-nine cents. Teenagers these days, they just don't have any concept of customer service. My nephew is looking for a job right now, he's sixteen, and I told his mother she needs to teach him how to look people in the eye and shake hands properly. But she just rolls her eyes at me. She always was the stubborn one in the family. We used to fight over the bathroom when we were girls...

But no, it hasn't been going on for months and months after things settled. It's just all still connected to her death and that luncheon we never got to finish.

patient.answer:
Accepting it? Well... I know she's gone, if that's what you mean. I saw her in the casket, after all. They did a lovely job with her hair, really. Usually, funeral directors just spray it stiff as a board, like a helmet. I remember when my Uncle Arthur passed, they parted his hair on the wrong side. He always wore it parted on the left, ever since he was in the Navy. He served on a destroyer, you know. The USS... oh, I can't recall the name, but he brought back the most beautiful silk kimono for my aunt from Japan. It was a deep emerald green with gold thread embroidered all over it, little cranes flying. She kept it in a cedar chest at the foot of her bed. Cedar smells so wonderful, doesn't it? It keeps the moths away, too. Although, I've heard you can use lavender sachets for that now. I tried growing lavender once by the front porch, but the soil was too acidic or something, it just withered right up. The lady at the garden center said I should have tested the pH first... 

But yes, I know she's gone. I just... I haven't quite figured out what to do with myself without her, I suppose.
